subject: physics
title: Life cycle of stars
key_idea: A star forms from a nebula and is stable while gravity is balanced by the outward pressure from fusion. A star like the Sun becomes a red giant and then a white dwarf. A more massive star ends in a supernova and leaves a neutron star or black hole.

blocks.text: (Physics only, not needed for Combined Science) A star goes through a life cycle. How it ends depends on its mass.

items.meaning: A cloud of dust and gas, mostly hydrogen.
A star forming as the nebula is pulled together by gravity.
A stable star fusing hydrogen into helium.
Small nuclei join to form larger nuclei, releasing energy.

items: Gravity pulls a nebula together, so the temperature rises.
When it is hot enough, nuclear fusion begins and a main sequence star forms.
Hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium nuclei.

blocks.text: A main sequence star is stable. The inward force of gravity is balanced by the outward forces from the energy released in fusion.

items: A nebula collapses under gravity until it is hot enough for fusion.
A main sequence star is stable because gravity and fusion are in equilibrium.

sections.heading: Stars similar in mass to the Sun

blocks.text: When the hydrogen in the core begins to run out, the balance changes and the star leaves the main sequence.

items: The star expands to become a **red giant**.
It throws off its outer layers of gas (a planetary nebula) and the core collapses to become a **white dwarf**.
The white dwarf cools to become a black dwarf.

diagram.alt: Put the life cycle of a star similar in mass to the Sun in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the life cycle of a star like the Sun in order.

items: A star like the Sun becomes a red giant, then a white dwarf, then a black dwarf.
The order of the stages matters in an answer.

sections.heading: Stars much more massive than the Sun

blocks.text: A star much more massive than the Sun starts in the same way, but ends differently.

items: After the main sequence it expands to become a red super giant.
It then collapses rapidly and explodes in a **supernova**.
It leaves behind a neutron star or a black hole.

diagram.alt: The life cycle of a star much more massive than the Sun.

items: Fusion in stars produces all the naturally occurring elements.
Hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium. Helium nuclei fuse to make heavier elements, up to iron.
Elements heavier than iron are produced in a supernova.
The explosion distributes the elements throughout the Universe.
A massive star becomes a red super giant, then a supernova, then a neutron star or black hole.
Stars make elements up to iron by fusion.
Elements heavier than iron form in a supernova, which spreads them through the Universe.

checks.q: Explain why a main sequence star is stable.
checks.a: The inward force of gravity is balanced (in equilibrium) with the outward forces caused by the energy released in nuclear fusion.

checks.q: Describe what happens to a star the size of the Sun after the main sequence stage. Name the stages.
checks.a: It expands to become a red giant, then collapses to become a white dwarf, then cools to become a black dwarf.

checks.q: State where elements heavier than iron are made.
checks.a: In a supernova, the explosion of a massive star.

worked_example.question:
A main sequence star in a distant galaxy is the same size and mass as the Sun.

Describe what will happen to the star between the main sequence stage and the end of the star's life cycle.
You should include the names of the stages in the life cycle of the star.
answer_points: The star will expand to become a red giant.
The star will collapse to become a white dwarf.
The star will cool to become a black dwarf.
worked_example.tip: The stages must be in the correct sequence to score all three marks.

worked_example.question:
During the evolution of a star, the nebula collapses and becomes a main sequence star.

Explain why the nebula stops collapsing as it becomes a main sequence star.
answer_points: Gravity causes an increase in temperature.
Until it is hot enough for fusion.
Until there is a balance between gravity and fusion (thermal expansion).
worked_example.tip: Allow increase in pressure or density, nuclear reactions, or equilibrium. Fission is ignored.

worked_example.question:
It is difficult for nuclear fusion reactions to occur on Earth.

Explain why nuclear fusion reactions occur in the Sun.
answer_points: Large gravitational forces (due to its large mass).
Any two of these score the marks.
worked_example.tip: Any two points score. 'Heat' is ignored.

worked_example.question:
Approximately 4.6 billion years ago, the Sun formed from an interstellar cloud of gas and became a stable star.
Describe and explain what happens as a protostar becomes a stable star.
answer_points: Nuclear fusion (nuclear reactions) begins in the star.
The gravitational force is inwards and the outward force is due to the high temperature.

items: The Sun is a medium-sized star, made mostly of hydrogen and helium.
The Sun radiates most of its energy as infrared, visible light and ultraviolet.
(Supplement) Stars are powered by nuclear reactions that release energy. In a stable star, hydrogen fuses into helium.
(Supplement) A supernova forms a nebula containing hydrogen and new heavier elements. This nebula may form new stars with planets orbiting them.

worked_example.question: Describe the stages in the evolution of a star similar in mass to the Sun.
answer_points: A nebula (cloud of dust and gas) becomes a protostar.
The protostar becomes a main sequence star.
The main sequence star becomes a red giant.
The red giant becomes a white dwarf, which finally cools to a black dwarf.
worked_example.tip: Give the stages in the correct order and link each to the next.

blocks.text: An HR diagram plots the brightness (luminosity) of stars against their surface temperature. The temperature axis runs backwards: hot on the left, cool on the right.

items: Most stars lie on a band from the hot, bright top left to the cool, dim bottom right. This is the main sequence.
Red giants and red supergiants are cool and very bright, at the top right.
White dwarfs are hot and dim, at the bottom left.
